V-ENCLOSURE.evidence: The garden consists of open ground with scattered plantings and no defined outdoor rooms with enclosing edges.

V-FOCAL.evidence: Large blue pond in the upper right quadrant serves as the dominant visual anchor, with surrounding planting and paving directing attention towards it.

V-AXIS.evidence: Paved areas connect the house door to the garden court, pond, and seating areas; no paths lead to blank edges or dead ends.

V-RHYTHM.evidence: Multiple groups of identical circles (shrubs and small trees) are clustered together in distinct beds on the left, top, and bottom right, indicating mass planting and repetition.

V-LAYERING.evidence: Canopy trees (e.g., Olea, Punica) are layered over shrubs and ground/perennials in the left and right planting beds, creating distinct vertical layers.

V-ROOMS.evidence: Distinct areas include a paved pond terrace, a garden court with different paving, and multiple planting beds with shrubs and trees, creating a sequence of spaces.

V-OVERALL.evidence: Distinct planting beds with defined edges, a central paved garden court, a pond feature, and grouped planting masses create clear spatial structure and rooms.
